questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Economic aspects. Would not have been able to do it without the erasmus grant. Great culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wrote to the study abroad office at my receiving univeristy a couple of times, and they were always very helpfull, and quick reply aways.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The hosted a great intro day where you got all the relevant and important information. Very informative.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult and very expensive. More help would be nice. I rented through airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Expensive but besides that I had a great landlord
Maybe some roomates you dont know beforehand

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Via their website. In the first one or two weeks it was possible to change course without any problems. This means that the students dont really have to choose beforehand since the first week is dedicated to trying different courses, so you are able to select the best one for you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was both a fysical office where you could seek help, but also via email - quick and helpful always. The teachers was also very helpfull and kind.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: All first priorities accepted, I dont think they have a limit - they will figure it out so all the students gets the course they want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a very relaxed procedure. Dont worry if you dont know before starting your exchange.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: good variation in the courses. The level was not that difficult. Not much preparation is required.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In my home university we have to do a lot more preparation before each lesson. We read a lot on our own, and use a lot of money on books. This was not the case at the host institution.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Arbitration 
EU law before courts 
European private law 
Data protection law 
International organizations and human rights

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I think that the course European private law was good because broad - we learned about european competition law, data protection law, consumer law, UNIDROIT and more. 
I would also recommend international arbitration.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: 100 euros to the erasmus student organization if you want to join the intro week

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Expensive to use the trains to other cities. 
Not very expensive to eat out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont know since it did not use them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I know that there were different soccer teams and match padel - there was probably more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I dont know since it did not use these kinds of services at my host institution.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: To explore the country - not just the city where you live.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult since you dont really get integrated with local students - just other international students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No since I did not get to socialize with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very relaxed and not that stringent.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Very great facilities - it is a private university. 
Get ahead of the game when it comes to housing - the sooner the better 
Just ask for help if in doubt - they are super nice

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Being on your own and making it work 
Always good weather and amazing culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making everyday life work when it's only temporary

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: look forward to it and enjoy it, it's over quickly

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
